title: Integrated metabolomics and mass spectrometry imaging reveal cultivar‐specific metabolic profiles and spatial distribution patterns in guava (Psidium guajava L.) fruit
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Guava (Psidium guajava L.) exhibits substantial cultivar-associated variation in fruit composition; however, the metabolic differences between cultivars and their spatial organization during fruit development remain incompletely understood. This study compared mature pulp of ‘Hongbaoshi’ (GH) and ‘Yanzhihong’ (GY) using ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS/MS)-based metabolomic profiling and targeted quantification, and visualized selected metabolite-related ions across fruit developmental stages by gold nanoparticle (AuNP)-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (LDI-MSI).

RESULTS

UPLC–MS/MS-based metabolomic profiling detected 569 metabolites, of which 199 were classified as differentially accumulated metabolites based on |log2Fold Change| > 1, P < 0.05, and variable importance in projection (VIP) > 1. The two cultivars showed distinct metabolite profiles involving amino acids, phenolic acids, flavonoids, organic acids, lipids, and sugars and alcohols. Targeted amino acid quantification showed higher glutamic acid, aspartic acid, glutamine, lysine, and alanine contents in GH, whereas phenylalanine, tryptophan, isoleucine, and proline were higher in GY. Glucose and sucrose were significantly higher in GH, whereas fructose was significantly higher in GY (q < 0.05). Qualitative LDI-MSI further revealed developmental-stage-associated spatial patterns of selected sugar-, amino-acid-, and organic-acid-related ions. Several signals tended to localize more strongly in the central pulp of representative GY sections, whereas corresponding signals in GH were more broadly distributed.

CONCLUSION

Integration of metabolomic profiling, targeted quantification, and spatial imaging revealed distinct cultivar-associated metabolic characteristics and developmental spatial patterns in guava fruit, providing biochemical and spatial information relevant to fruit-quality evaluation and germplasm characterization. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
